title: 2025 record for Chinese coast guard presence near Senkakus
detail: Japan Coast Guard data reported Chinese coast guard vessels were sighted near the Senkakus 357 times in 2025, a record for the fourth straight year, with 27 entries into territorial waters. The 11th Regional Coast Guard commander called the situation 'increasingly severe'.
attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

title: Record ~6kg meth seizure at Naha Airport announced
detail: Okinawa District Customs and prefectural police said a 27-year-old man arriving from Bangkok (Don Mueang) on Sept 30, 2025 carried about 5.95kg of methamphetamine, worth about ¥340 million, in candy and detergent boxes; the largest seizure at Naha Airport.
agency: Okinawa District Customs / Okinawa Prefectural Police
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa District Customs / Okinawa Prefectural Police

title: Six including Kyokuryukai executive held over labour dispatch to US base sites
detail: Organized crime police arrested six people including a senior figure of designated gang Kyokuryukai, alleging 25 workers were illegally dispatched 819 times to 114 sites incl. Kadena Air Base and public works between April 2023 and July 2025.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police

title: Four Chinese warships transit Miyako Strait
detail: Japan's Maritime Self-Defense Force tracked two Chinese guided-missile destroyers, a frigate and a replenishment ship passing between Okinawa and Miyako Island into the Philippine Sea overnight (Tuesday evening to early Wednesday), per Japan's Joint Staff.
attribution: Japan Joint Staff via Stars and Stripes

title: Three foreigners caught with THC gummies at Naha Airport
detail: Customs found THC gummies on a Brazilian couple resident in Okinawa City (2.18g) and a US man from Michigan (~78g) arriving from Bangkok; all three were arrested/charged under the narcotics law, with charges filed by customs.
agency: Okinawa District Customs / Tomigusuku Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa District Customs / Tomigusuku Police Station

title: Foam from sewer manhole near Futenma prompts PFAS tests
detail: Ginowan's sewage division received a report of white foam coming from a manhole in the Isa district that collects water from MCAS Futenma and nearby homes; city and US military took samples for PFAS testing. Marines said there had been no firefighting-foam releases.
attribution: Ginowan City via Stars and Stripes

title: Four Chinese coast guard ships enter Senkaku territorial waters
detail: Four China Coast Guard ships entered Japanese territorial waters near Uotsuri Island and Taisho islet shortly after 4 p.m. and left about two hours later; the Japan Coast Guard said it was the second incursion of 2026 and that no Japanese fishing boats were being pursued.
attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

title: Okinawa fraud losses about ¥3.2 billion in 2025
detail: National Police Agency figures released Feb 12 put 2025 losses to special fraud plus SNS investment and romance scams at a record ~¥324.1 billion nationwide (+62.8%), with Okinawa losses about ¥3.2 billion.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing National Police Agency

title: Kyokuryukai chairman arrested for attempted extortion
detail: Police arrested the 71-year-old chairman of designated gang Kyokuryukai and a 45-year-old member on suspicion of attempting to extort 'settlement money' from a woman in her 50s over an August 2024 container-confinement incident.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station

title: US Marine arrested for trespassing at elementary school
detail: Okinawa police arrested a 21-year-old Marine corporal from Camp Schwab on suspicion of entering an elementary school in northern Okinawa without permission; witnesses said he spoke to and followed a young girl, and police detected alcohol. He denied the allegation.
attribution: Okinawa police via Xinhua

title: Ex-couple arrested over cashing ~¥100m of bonds stolen from vacant house
detail: Police allege two residents of Haebaru bought bonds that juveniles had stolen from a vacant house in Okinawa and redeemed them for about ¥100 million at a Tokyo financial institution in Aug 2025; charges include receiving stolen goods and fraud. Over ¥100 million in cash was also reportedly found at the house.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station

title: Third arrest in stolen-bond laundering case
detail: A 27-year-old man from Itoman was arrested as a third suspect; police allege violations of the Act on Punishment of Organized Crimes (concealment and receipt of criminal proceeds) and fraud over roughly ¥100 million in redeemed stolen bonds, allegedly spent on dining and luxury goods.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station

title: Naha man sentenced for receiving fraud and theft proceeds
detail: The Naha District Court Okinawa Branch sentenced a 34-year-old Naha man to 1 year 6 months' imprisonment and a ¥500,000 fine for knowingly receiving ¥905,000 of criminal proceeds on five occasions under the organized crime law; prosecutors had sought 2 years.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Naha District Court Okinawa Branch

title: Prefectural police and six lenders agree to share fraud-account data
detail: Okinawa Prefectural Police signed an agreement with Ryukyu Bank, Bank of Okinawa, Okinawa Kaiho Bank, Koza Shinkin, Okinawa Rokin and JA Okinawa to share details of frozen fraud-linked accounts in real time. Police cited 543 fraud cases and about ¥3.23 billion in losses in the prefecture last year.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police and participating banks

title: Chinese coast guard ships chase Japanese fishing boat into Senkaku waters
detail: Two China Coast Guard vessels entered territorial waters about 12 nautical miles southwest of Minamikojima around 5:30 a.m. while pursuing a Japanese fishing boat and stayed until 7:20 p.m. the next day; two more ships were in the contiguous zone, per Japan Coast Guard releases.
attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

title: Two boats capsize off Henoko on school peace trip; 2 dead
detail: Two small motorboats carrying Kyoto high school students capsized off Henoko Cape near Camp Schwab at 10:10 a.m.; a 17-year-old student and a captain in his 70s died. The coast guard sent 11 boats and a helicopter.
attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

title: Body found after sugarcane field fire in Miyakojima
detail: A fire burned about 4,000 sq m of a sugarcane field in Taira, Miyakojima; a man's body was found and the 90-year-old owner could not be reached.
agency: Miyakojima Police Station / Miyakojima City Fire Department
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Miyakojima Police Station / Miyakojima City Fire Department

title: Second Chinese coast guard incursion at Senkakus in same week
detail: Four China Coast Guard vessels, including the pair from Monday's incursion, re-entered Japanese territorial waters shortly after 4 p.m. and left after about two hours; Japanese patrol ships warned them with electronic message boards, according to the Japan Coast Guard (fifth incursion of 2026).
attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

title: US sailor gets suspended sentence for mailing magic truffles to Okinawa
detail: Naha District Court gave a Camp Foster-based US Navy petty officer a two-year sentence suspended for four years for trying to import 71g of psilocybin truffles by mail from the Netherlands.
attribution: Stars and Stripes, citing Naha District Court

title: Prefectural survey finds record PFAS near Kadena and Futenma
detail: Okinawa's environmental division reported new maximum PFAS levels, up to 2,800 ppt at Yara Hijaga in Kadena town (standard 50 ppt), with elevated levels at 31 of 44 sites around US bases including downstream of Futenma.
attribution: Okinawa Prefecture via Stars and Stripes

title: Chinese research ship surveys in Japan's EEZ near Senkakus
detail: The Chinese research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 22 was found about 40 miles west-northwest of Uotsuri Island extending pipe- and wire-like objects into the sea in Japan's EEZ; a Japan Coast Guard patrol ship radioed that research without Japan's consent was unacceptable.
attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

title: Four armed Chinese coast guard ships briefly enter Senkaku waters
detail: Maritime Executive, citing a Japan Coast Guard statement, reported four China Coast Guard ships (Haijing 2303, 2302, 2401, 2307), observed with machine guns, were in territorial waters from about 06:00 to 06:20, and that Chinese vessels had been present around the Senkakus for 138 consecutive days.
attribution: Japan Coast Guard via The Maritime Executive

title: First measles case of 2026 in Okinawa
detail: Okinawa Prefecture reported its first measles patient of 2026 and warned people who shared air space at locations the patient visited that they may have been exposed.
agency: Okinawa Prefecture Health and Medical Care Dept.
attribution: Okinawa Prefectural Government

title: Kin town water survey finds PFAS near Camp Hansen
detail: Kin town's annual survey found five of 14 sites above Japan's 50 ppt standard, highest 220 ppt near Ryukyu Hospital about 730 feet from Camp Hansen; the water is not used for drinking.
attribution: Kin Town via Stars and Stripes

title: Influenza advisory lifted (week 14)
detail: Okinawa Prefecture lifted its influenza advisory as reports fell to 6.64 per sentinel site in week 14 (Mar 30-Apr 5), but said Yaeyama still exceeded the threshold.
attribution: Okinawa Prefectural Government

title: Taiwanese cruise passenger caught with stimulants at Naha Port
detail: A 56-year-old Taiwanese national arriving on a cruise ship from Keelung was found with 1.2g of stimulants; Naha Coast Guard arrested him April 12 and customs filed charges April 27.
agency: Okinawa District Customs / Naha Coast Guard Office
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa District Customs / Naha Coast Guard Office

title: Chinese research vessel Kexue operates in EEZ north of Ishigaki
detail: The Chinese research ship Kexue was spotted about 45 miles north of Ishigaki extending wire-like objects until April 17, then stayed in Japan's EEZ until leaving westward early on April 29, the third such case in a month, per the Japan Coast Guard.
attribution: Japan Coast Guard via Stars and Stripes

title: Chinese destroyer and frigate pass south of Hateruma
detail: Japan's Joint Staff Office reported destroyer Baotou and frigate Huanggang operating in the southwest region between April 19 and 22, including a passage about 80 km south of Hateruma Island.
attribution: Japan Joint Staff Office via USNI News

title: Fatal fire at gang office flat in Okinawa City
detail: A pre-dawn fire gutted a fourth-floor flat in Moromizato used as an office of designated gang Kyokuryukai; one person died and police were checking whether it was the group's chairman, who could not be reached.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police

title: Russian submarine and warships transit near Yonaguni
detail: Japan's Joint Staff Office reported a Russian group (submarine Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, corvette Gromkiy, a tug) sailing about 50 km south of Yonaguni on April 21, and a second group (corvettes Sovershenny and Rezkiy, oiler Pechenga) passing between Yonaguni and Iriomote into the East China Sea around midnight on April 22.
attribution: Japan Joint Staff Office via USNI News

title: FY2025 scrambles: Southwestern Air Defense Force handles 348
detail: Japan's Joint Staff annual report says ASDF fighters scrambled 595 times in FY2025 (about 366 against Chinese aircraft), with the Okinawa-based Southwestern Air Defense Force conducting 348; it cites a Chinese coast guard helicopter entering airspace around the Senkakus in May 2025.
srcname: Japan Ministry of Defense Joint Staff
attribution: Japan Joint Staff Office

title: Survey finds PFAS up to 3,000 ppt downstream of Futenma
detail: Okinawa's groundwater surveys found PFAS at 28 of 40 sites near MCAS Futenma, peaking at 3,000 ppt at Ijunga spring, and up to 400 ppt near Camp Kinser; the prefecture said the base is highly probably the source.
attribution: Okinawa Prefecture via Stars and Stripes

title: Prefecture issues school-trip safety notice after capsizing
detail: Okinawa Prefecture asked organizers of school trips to adopt safety measures to prevent a recurrence after the fatal capsizing of boats carrying an out-of-prefecture high school group.
attribution: Okinawa Prefectural Government

title: Marine dies in motorcycle-taxi crash on Route 58 near Camp Kinser
detail: A 21-year-old Marine riding south on Route 58 in Urasoe's Yafuso district collided with a turning taxi at 12:45 a.m. near Camp Kinser's Gate 2 and was declared dead around 1:30 a.m., police and the Marine Corps said.
attribution: Stars and Stripes

title: Two US Marines arrested for hotel break-in and drunk driving
detail: Okinawa police arrested two Marines on Sunday, one on suspicion of breaking into a hotel and the other for suspected drunk driving; both denied the allegations. Xinhua noted Okinawa police handled over 100 criminal cases involving US personnel in 2025.
attribution: Okinawa police via Xinhua

title: Second, unrelated measles case in Okinawa
detail: Okinawa Prefecture reported its second measles case of 2026, not linked to the first, and warned people who may have been exposed.
agency: Okinawa Prefecture Health and Medical Care Dept.
attribution: Okinawa Prefectural Government

title: Four Chinese coast guard ships enter waters off Uotsuri
detail: Four China Coast Guard ships entered Japanese territorial waters near Uotsuri Island between 4:15 and 4:35 p.m. and left around 6 p.m., the first such entry since April 28, Jiji Press reported.
attribution: Jiji Press

title: Aichi man re-arrested over cash-card fraud against elderly women in Yomitan, Chatan
detail: Okinawa police re-arrested a 21-year-old Aichi company employee who allegedly posed as a municipal official offering insurance refunds, obtained cash cards from two women in their 70s and withdrew about ¥450,000 on April 8.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Okinawa Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Okinawa Police Station

title: Four Vietnamese arrested for shipping 1,936 protected hermit crabs
detail: Naha police arrested four Vietnamese nationals for allegedly shipping 1,936 land hermit crabs, a designated natural monument, out of the prefecture from a Naha convenience store under the Cultural Properties Protection Act; a courier had alerted police.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station

title: 250kg US bomb defused in Urasoe; 850 evacuated, monorail halted
detail: The JGSDF defused a US-made 250kg bomb near Urasoe-Maeda station; about 850 people were evacuated within 283m and Yui Rail was suspended between Shuri and Urasoe for about 2h45m.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Japan Ground Self-Defense Force

title: US soldier referred to prosecutors over alleged sexual assault
detail: Okinawa Prefectural Police referred a Kadena-based US Army air-defense soldier in his 20s to the Naha prosecutors over an alleged April sexual assault and injury of a woman outdoors on Okinawa's main island; he also allegedly hit a roadside barrier and failed to report it.
attribution: Okinawa police via Stars and Stripes

title: TB cluster at adult day-care facility in southern Okinawa
detail: The prefecture announced a tuberculosis cluster at an adult day-care facility under the Southern Health Center: as of May 11, 5 active cases and 27 infections.
attribution: Okinawa Prefectural Government

title: Tropical Storm Jangmi crosses Okinawa
detail: Jiji reported a maximum gust of 30.7 m/s in Naha on June 1 as Jangmi was forecast to cross the main island; JMA urged residents to avoid nonessential travel. Wikipedia's compilation lists 17 injuries and 82,921 evacuated across five municipalities in Okinawa.
attribution: JMA via Jiji Press; injury/evacuation figures from Wikipedia

title: Jangmi cuts power in 27 Okinawa municipalities
detail: Power outages affected 27 municipalities in Okinawa Prefecture as Tropical Storm Jangmi crossed the islands, according to Wikipedia's storm article.
attribution: Wikipedia (secondary compilation)

title: Tsunami advisory reaches Okinawa after M7.8 Philippines quake
detail: JMA issued a tsunami advisory from Ibaraki to Okinawa after a magnitude 7.8 quake off the southern Philippines, earlier warning of up to 1 m for Miyako and Yaeyama; a minor tsunami was observed on Okinawa's main island around 12:18 p.m.
attribution: JMA via Inquirer

title: Three Chinese nationals held over underground bank laundering Okinawa fraud money
detail: A joint Tokyo MPD-Okinawa police task force arrested two Tokyo-based Chinese nationals on June 8 for unlicensed currency exchange (Banking Act) and a third on June 15 for fraud; police suspect special-fraud proceeds, including ¥5 million taken from an 80-year-old Okinawa resident, were laundered via the yuan-exchange scheme.
agency: Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department / Okinawa Prefectural Police
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing MPD-Okinawa joint investigation

title: First UXO disposal on Yonaguni: four WWII navy bombs
detail: Four 250kg Imperial Japanese Navy bombs found offshore in 2020 were disposed of underwater near Kubura port, with a 3km diving ban and vessel limits.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo

title: Four US servicemen arrested in two days in Okinawa
detail: Okinawa police arrested two US servicemen for alleged drunk driving on June 13 and, on June 14, one for an assault at a restaurant that injured a person's head and one for trespassing in an apartment building.
attribution: Xinhua, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police

title: Level 4 heavy-rain and landslide warnings on Okinawa Island; Tonaki 73mm/h
detail: The Okinawa Meteorological Observatory issued heavy-rain warnings for Tonaki and Motobu and landslide warnings for Urasoe, Nanjo, Yaese, Kitanakagusuku and Onna; Tonaki logged 73mm in an hour and a record 205.5mm in 6 hours. Naha had 382.5mm from June 9-16.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Meteorological Observatory (JMA)

title: Floods and landslides across Okinawa Island; cars submerged
detail: Heavy rain submerged three cars in about 1m of water in Okinawa City, stranded two on Route 54 in Itoman and flooded Route 449 in Motobu; landslides hit Miyagi Island (Uruma), Nakijin and Urasoe. Evacuation centres opened; no deaths reported.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo

title: Resolute Dragon 26 drills include Sakishima disaster-relief training
detail: Japan's defense ministry said the Japan-US Resolute Dragon 26 exercise (June 20-30) would set up command centers at Camp Foster and Camp Kinser and hold disaster-relief drills on Miyako (about 70 personnel), Ishigaki (about 50) and Yonaguni (about 50) with Ospreys, CH-47s, CH-53s and C-130s.
place: Camp Foster / Camp Kinser; Miyako, Ishigaki, Yonaguni
attribution: Japan MoD via USNI News

title: Trash burning spreads, five houses burn down in Nago
detail: Five homes in the Umusa area of Nago were destroyed after a resident's trash fire spread; no injuries were reported.
agency: Nago Fire Department / Nago Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Nago Fire Department / Nago Police Station

title: Fake-police scam takes ¥200,000 in crypto from northern Okinawa woman
detail: Callers posing as out-of-prefecture police and prosecutors told a woman in her 40s her cash card was found at a suspect's home and had her buy and send about ¥200,000 in cryptocurrency, Nago police said.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Nago Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Nago Police Station

title: Central Okinawa firm loses ¥27.3m to CEO-impersonation email
detail: An employee of a company in central Okinawa wired ¥27.3 million after an email in the CEO's name led her to a LINE group demanding payment, Urasoe police said, urging firms to verify remittance rules.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Urasoe Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Urasoe Police Station

title: Chinese national caught near fishing port as fake-police scam collector in Kin
detail: Ishikawa police arrested a 48-year-old Chinese national on July 1 (re-arrested July 22) as the alleged cash collector in a fake-police scam in which a Kin man in his 40s left ¥1.5 million in his mailbox; he tried to flee toward a fishing port when a second ¥2 million pickup was staked out.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Ishikawa Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Ishikawa Police Station

title: Hermit-crab poachers fined; 3,869 crabs taken
detail: Four Vietnamese nationals were fined ¥300,000-400,000 each by summary order after prosecutors charged them over collecting and shipping 3,869 protected land hermit crabs, many juveniles.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Naha District Public Prosecutors Office

title: M6.1-6.4 quake northwest of Miyako Island
detail: An offshore quake northwest of Miyakojima (about 26N 125.8E) was rated M6.4 by JMA (M6.1 by USGS), shaking Kume Island at lower 3; no tsunami warning or damage was reported.
attribution: JMA via SANA; USGS figure via Yeni Safak

title: Man arrested after violent assault at Naha seaside park
detail: Police arrested a 35-year-old man on suspicion of assault after a 23-year-old man was badly beaten at Wakasa Seaside Park near Naminoue Beach; off-duty US Marines gave first aid and held the suspect until police arrived.
attribution: Stars and Stripes

title: Japan and China coast guards face off near Senkakus
detail: Two of four China Coast Guard ships entered waters near the Senkakus; Japan's coast guard said it forced them out by about 9:20 a.m., while China's coast guard said it had expelled the Japanese fishing boat Zuihou Maru. Tokyo called the entry a violation of international law.
attribution: Japan Coast Guard and China Coast Guard statements via The Defense Post (AFP)

title: Typhoon Bavi hits Sakishima islands
detail: Bavi (950 hPa, up to 40 m/s sustained) brought gusts of 40 m/s on Miyako and 34 m/s on Ishigaki early July 11; Shimoji Island recorded 154.5 mm of rain in 24 hours, Jiji reported.
attribution: JMA via Jiji Press

title: Hand, foot and mouth disease warning issued
detail: Okinawa Prefecture issued a hand, foot and mouth disease warning as week 28 (Jul 6-12) reports reached 5.29 per sentinel (threshold 5.00), 127 cases from 24 sites; first warning in about two years.
attribution: Okinawa Prefectural Government

title: Japan's first case under new 'remittance crime' law, in Tomigusuku
detail: Tomigusuku police referred a Tomigusuku woman in her 40s to prosecutors, the first case nationwide under the Criminal Proceeds Transfer Prevention Act's new remittance-offence provision (in force July 10). She allegedly took an Instagram 'side job', received about ¥1.75 million and forwarded it to designated accounts; her bank flagged the activity.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Tomigusuku Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Tomigusuku Police Station

title: Store staff stop lottery-prize fraud against elderly man
detail: Staff at a Tomigusuku convenience store stopped an elderly customer from buying a prepaid card (¥3,000 'handling fee') for a fake ¥700 million prize and called police; Tomigusuku Police commended them. Police said such special-fraud schemes escalate from small initial payments.
attribution: Tomigusuku Police via SoraNews24

title: Okinawa special-fraud losses about ¥1.2 billion in first half of 2026
detail: National Police Agency figures put first-half 2026 special-fraud losses at a record ~¥181.6 billion nationwide, with Okinawa losses reported at about ¥1.2 billion.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing National Police Agency

title: Uruma teen arrested for cannabis possession
detail: Uruma police arrested an 18-year-old man over 2.47g of cannabis found in a store parking lot on July 9, then re-arrested him for use after a positive urine test.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Uruma Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Uruma Police Station

title: US consulate warns of large typhoon, closes Aug 6-7
detail: The US Consulate General Naha warned that a large typhoon would affect Okinawa from Aug. 6 through at least Aug. 9 with very strong winds, storm surge, heavy rain, flooding and landslides, and closed to the public Aug. 6-7.
attribution: US Consulate General Naha

title: Typhoon Dolphin strengthens near northwestern Okinawa
detail: JMA data showed 10-minute sustained winds of 162 km/h; gusts reached 151 km/h in Nago and at Oku (Kunigami). The prefecture reported at least five injured and partial damage to five homes; evacuation orders covered about 262,500 people across Kagoshima and Okinawa.
attribution: JMA and Okinawa Prefecture via The Watchers

title: Level 4 heavy-rain warnings for Ogimi, Higashi, Nakijin
detail: During Typhoon Dolphin, JMA Level 4 heavy-rain risk warnings were in effect for Ogimi, Higashi and Nakijin in northern Okinawa Island.
attribution: JMA via The Watchers

title: Level 4 storm-surge warning for Kumejima
detail: During Typhoon Dolphin a JMA Level 4 storm-surge risk warning was in effect for Kumejima.
attribution: JMA via The Watchers

title: Typhoon Dolphin leaves about 17,000 households without power
detail: About 16,920 households in 21 municipalities were without power at 17:00 JST, roughly 90% of them in northern Okinawa Island (AFP/ABC reported about 12,000-14,000 buildings the following day).
attribution: The Watchers

title: All 417 flights at Naha, Miyako, Ishigaki, Shimojishima cancelled
detail: All 417 scheduled flights serving Naha, Miyako, Ishigaki and Shimojishima airports on Aug. 7 were cancelled because of Typhoon Dolphin.
attribution: The Watchers

title: Pre-dawn fire at Chatan hotel; unconscious guest rescued
detail: Police got a report of a hotel fire in Chatan at 3:30 a.m.; a Marine alerted sleeping guests and firefighters removed an unconscious 55-year-old man. Police later alleged a guest set the fire deliberately.
attribution: Stars and Stripes

title: Man in 20s loses ¥6.7m to fake police via LINE video call
detail: Scammers posing as police and prosecutors showed a fake warrant over LINE video and had a self-employed man in his 20s in central Okinawa transfer about ¥6.7 million between Aug 4 and 17, Ginowan police said.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Ginowan Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Ginowan Police Station

title: Typhoon Saudel lashes Okinawa and Amami
detail: Saudel carried winds up to 144 km/h; a 78-year-old woman in Uruma was injured when wind knocked her down, about 150 Naha flights were cancelled, and up to 12 cm of rain was forecast for Okinawa, per JMA, FDMA and prefectural officials cited by AP.
attribution: AP citing JMA, FDMA, prefectural officials

title: About 150 Naha flights cancelled for Typhoon Saudel
detail: Some 150 flights to and from Naha Airport were cancelled as Typhoon Saudel passed near Okinawa, AP reported.
attribution: AP

title: American tourist arrested over alleged arson at Chatan hotel
detail: Okinawa police arrested a 32-year-old US visitor with no fixed address on suspicion of arson and attempted murder over the Aug. 15 fire at a Chatan hotel where 18 other guests were staying; he was already in custody over an Aug. 21 break-in in Urasoe.
attribution: Okinawa police via Stars and Stripes

title: Fake arrest-warrant scam costs southern Okinawa worker ¥800,000
detail: A company employee in his 30s in southern Okinawa main island sent about ¥800,000 after callers posing as police and prosecutors claimed a warrant was out for him, Naha police said.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Naha Police Station

title: Illegal insect traps found again in Yanbaru National Park
detail: The Environment Ministry and prefectural police found 16 unauthorised insect traps targeting rare species in Yanbaru (Kunigami, Ogimi, Higashi) so far in FY2026, after 25 in FY2025, and are stepping up countermeasures.
agency: Ministry of the Environment / Okinawa Prefectural Police
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Ministry of the Environment / Okinawa Prefectural Police

title: Downpour floods roads on Ishigaki, two cars submerged
detail: 48.5mm fell in an hour in Maesato, Ishigaki; two cars were submerged, a road flooded about 50cm deep and was closed, and a waste facility briefly halted. The observatory linked instability to typhoons 18 and 24 nearby.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Ishigaki Local Meteorological Office (JMA)

title: Southwestern ASDF scrambles on Chinese Y-9 near Okinawa
detail: Japan's Joint Staff said a Chinese Y-9 intelligence aircraft flew over the East China Sea five days running (Sept 3-7) near Okinawa Island and the Danjo Islands; the Southwestern Air Defense Force scrambled on Sept 5. No airspace violation was reported.
place: East China Sea west of Okinawa Island
attribution: Japan Joint Staff Office via AeroTime

title: Kanagawa man arrested as withdrawer in ¥3m refund scam on northern Okinawa couple
detail: Police arrested a 50-year-old Kanagawa man, suspected withdrawer for an anonymous fluid-type crime group, over a scheme posing as city staff offering care-insurance refunds that took about ¥3 million from two people in their 60s in February; he denies the charges.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police

title: Saitama man arrested over ¥46m gold-bar fake-police scam in Naha
detail: Police arrested a 61-year-old Saitama man accused of posing as a police officer to collect gold bullion worth about ¥46 million from a Naha man in his 70s on July 1; police are probing an anonymous fluid-type crime group link and the gold's whereabouts.
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police

title: Camp Schwab Marine arrested for stealing car in Nago
detail: Nago police arrested a 21-year-old Marine lance corporal from Camp Schwab accused of stealing a car worth about ¥830,000 from a Nago parking lot; alcohol was detected and he reportedly said he took it to go to a convenience store.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Nago Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Nago Police Station

title: Influenza advisory issued; Okinawa highest per-sentinel in Japan
detail: Okinawa issued an influenza advisory as week 36 (Aug 31-Sep 6) reached 10.34 per sentinel (455 cases from 44 sites), the highest nationwide per Ryukyu Shimpo; Yaeyama (13.33) and the southern region (13.17) were highest.
attribution: Okinawa Prefectural Government; regional figures via Ryukyu Shimpo

title: Report says US told Japan in 2023 that base foam likely caused PFAS
detail: The Okinawa Times reported that US officials told Tokyo in December 2023 that PFAS foam used at Kadena and Futenma was likely responsible for nearby contamination, an assessment not made public; US and Japanese officials offered few details.
attribution: Okinawa Times via Stars and Stripes

title: Camp Hansen Marine arrested for drunk driving after crash in Okinawa City
detail: Okinawa police arrested a 22-year-old Camp Hansen Marine after a collision on Prefectural Route 23 in Ageda; a breath test showed 0.5mg/L or more of alcohol. He denies the charge.
agency: Okinawa Prefectural Police / Okinawa Police Station
attribution: Ryukyu Shimpo, citing Okinawa Prefectural Police / Okinawa Police Station
